questions.q: Beyond a single pass/fail result, what does DBCC CHECKDB actually verify?
options: Allocation consistency, structural integrity, catalog consistency, and (with an option) data purity
Only whether the database can currently be backed up
Only disk free space on the database's drive
Only whether statistics are up to date
questions.explain: CHECKDB bundles several distinct checks: allocation, structural, catalog, and optionally data purity.

questions.q: What does the NO_INFOMSGS option do when added to a CHECKDB call?
options: Suppresses routine informational messages so a clean run produces no output
Skips the structural integrity check to run faster
Disables error reporting entirely
Forces CHECKDB to run in single-user mode
questions.explain: NO_INFOMSGS removes the routine informational chatter, which is why a silent run under this option means everything is clean.

questions.q: What does the DATA_PURITY option check for?
options: Column values that violate their declared data type's constraints
Whether index fragmentation exceeds a threshold
Whether the transaction log is full
Whether logins have appropriate permissions
questions.explain: DATA_PURITY checks for invalid column values, such as ones that don't fit their data type's constraints.

questions.q: Why does DATA_PURITY matter specifically for databases that trace back to very old SQL Server versions?
options: They don't get purity checks automatically until it's explicitly requested once, after which SQL Server flags them as purity-checked going forward
Old databases cannot run CHECKDB at all without this option
DATA_PURITY only works on databases created before SQL Server 2005
It rebuilds all indexes on databases from old SQL Server versions
questions.explain: Databases predating a certain point don't get automatic purity checks until DATA_PURITY is explicitly requested once; after that SQL Server runs it automatically.

questions.q: Why is DBCC CHECKDB usually run inside a scheduled Agent job rather than ad hoc?
options: It's I/O- and CPU-intensive on a large database, so it belongs in a maintenance window
CHECKDB can only be executed by SQL Server Agent, never interactively
It requires the database to be offline at all times
It automatically repairs any errors it finds without DBA review
questions.explain: CHECKDB's resource cost makes it a natural fit for a scheduled maintenance window, run as an unattended Agent job.
